## Measurement or a fixed scale? {#l1-precision }

**Define the variable before deciding.**

| Variable | What matters? |
|:---|:---|
| Actual running time, reported to 0.1 s | The underlying time is continuous. |
| An awarded ATAR on a 0.05 scale | The allowed ranks form a discrete set. |
| The final amount billed in whole cents | The payable amounts form a discrete set. |

::: {.takeaway}
Rounding a measurement does not change the underlying physical quantity.
:::

::: notes
Use precise language: if the variable is explicitly the rounded recorded number, its stored values lie on a discrete grid. If the variable is the actual physical measurement, model it as continuous. This distinction prepares students for the wording of Example 3.3; do not teach that every rounded measurement is inherently discrete.
:::
